rounds.text: Anirit Ventures Ltd demonstrates a clear commitment to balance sheet repair, evidenced by the successful reduction of borrowings from Rs 13.68 Cr to Rs 6.55 Cr over the last year [E27, E35]. This deleveraging effort provides a more stable foundation for future operations, especially as the company maintains a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.44x [E25]. Long-term shareholders have been rewarded with compounded share price growth of 51% over the last five years, indicating historical resilience [E16]. Furthermore, the company has shown the capacity for operational momentum, with recent screen data highlighting strong sales growth and quarterly profit improvements [E40, E41]. Conceded: [E13, E14, E19, E23, E24, E26]. While current metrics reflect a challenging period, the combination of active debt reduction and a stable promoter holding of 55.53% suggests a management team focused on navigating the company through its current transition [E27, E29].

The bull’s focus on debt reduction [E27, E35] ignores the reality that the company is currently facing a severe liquidity crisis, as evidenced by a current ratio of just 0.14x, meaning current liabilities vastly exceed current assets [E26]. While the bull highlights historical share price growth [E16], it fails to account for the catastrophic recent performance, including a 100% decline in compounded sales growth and a 184% drop in profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E13, E14]. The claim of operational momentum is directly contradicted by the company’s negative operating cash flow of Rs -6.82 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -6.76 Cr as of March 2026 [E23, E24]. Furthermore, the assertion that management is successfully navigating a transition is undermined by a staggering ROE of -141% and a quarterly operating margin that has deteriorated by 83 percentage points to -2733% [E12, E19]. Conceded: [E25, E27, E29]. Ultimately, the company’s valuation remains detached from its fundamental decay, as it trades at 3.94 times its book value despite generating negative returns on assets and capital [E7, E9, E36].
